drafts.title: 🛠️ Show Your Workflow: triaging an inbound NDA
drafts.body:
An NDA lands in the inbox at 6pm. The business wants it signed tomorrow. Most legal teams see dozens of these a month, and the first pass is where time disappears: reading counterparty paper, spotting what deviates from your positions, deciding what is worth a fight.

This week we want to see how you actually do it, with or without AI.

**Why this one**

NDA triage is a natural test case for agentic tools. Legora, for example, says its new **Skills** let teams save their standards as instructions the Agent applies, and its Skills Library lists an "Inbound NDA Triage" playbook with green, yellow and red tiers ([Legora: Skills](https://legora.com/product/skills); [Legora blog: Introducing Skills](https://legora.com/blog/introducing-skills); [Artificial Lawyer, 7 Oct 2026](https://artificiallawyer.com/2026/10/07/legora-launches-250-skills-for-legal-agents)). Whether you use Legora, another tool or a checklist and coffee, the logic is the same: the tool drafts, the lawyer decides.

**Reply template**

- **Context:** in-house or firm, rough volume per month, jurisdiction
- **Intake:** how NDAs reach you and who decides if legal even looks
- **First pass:** manual, playbook, AI tool (which one), or a mix
- **Your tiers:** what counts as green, yellow, red
- **Red flags:** the clauses you always check
- **Human check:** what you never let a tool decide alone
- **Time:** before vs after your current setup, honest estimate

**Example reply**

> **Context:** in-house, mid-size SaaS company, around 30 NDAs a month, mostly English law.
> **Intake:** sales submits via a form; mutual NDAs on our paper skip legal.
> **First pass:** AI review against a written playbook, then a 5-minute human read.
> **Tiers:** green = our template, or deviations within fallbacks. Yellow = non-standard term or residuals clause. Red = non-solicit, IP assignment, or one-way obligations on us.
> **Red flags:** definition of Confidential Information, term and survival, residuals, governing law.
> **Human check:** anything red, plus every redline that leaves the building.
> **Time:** from about 40 minutes to about 15 per NDA.

**Your turn**

Which clause does your process catch most often, and which one slipped through once?

Never paste confidential client data into public threads.
